changed_assumptions: Countable coded commutative rings, as required for the retained second-order arithmetic statement; no additional ring hypothesis. Only an upper bound on logical strength is proved.
statements.residual: No WKL0 reversal, lower bound on the optimal color count, or exact reverse-mathematical classification is proved.
findings: WKL0 proves the retained ring-coloring assertion over RCA0, with at most [3(n-1)]^(n-1) colors for n>=2 and one color for n<=1.
A finite-presentation construction avoids comprehension of the range sR; supplied finite integer matrices are diagonalized by an explicit primitive-recursive algorithm.
Every PA degree relative to the input can compute a witnessing coloring.
statements.source_status: The attachment records no exact closure; that historical statement is not itself a renewed literature search.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Determine liminf_(n→∞) Λ_(n,4) and limsup_(n→∞) Λ_(n,4), including whether they coincide.

auxiliary_results.statement: liminf Lambda_(n,4)>=50368/90905; exact nine-interval count R_(90905t)=2289351520t^2+25184t for every integer t>=1.

targets.exact_retained_statement: If no nonempty subset of the coefficients sums to zero, determine lim_(ε↓0)d(L,ε).

auxiliary_results.statement: For every fixed k>=3, c!=0, and epsilon>0, d(c(x1+...+xk)=0,epsilon)=1/k.
changed_assumptions: Equal coefficients.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Do absolute C,K>0 satisfy ω(G_p)≤C(log p)^K for every prime p≡1 mod 4?
Does some ε>0 satisfy SOS₄(G_p)=O(p^{1/2−ε}) as p→∞ through primes p≡1 mod 4?
Are there infinitely many such p with 1+τ₊(H_p)<⌊(1+√(2p−1))/2⌋?
Does there exist ε>0 such that θ(H_p)≤(1/√2−ε)√p for all sufficiently large primes p≡1 mod 4?
Do absolute C,α>0 and 0<δ<√2−1 exist such that (1−δ)||x||₂²≤||Φ_px||₂²≤(1+δ)||x||₂² for every x supported on at most Cp/(log p)^α coordinates and all sufficiently large such p?

auxiliary_results.statement: The two completed orthonormal character bases on the (p-1)-dimensional mean-zero space have overlap magnitude 1/sqrt(p-1); rs>=p-1. Every nonconstant rational function has full nonzero additive Fourier support.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Set F(n)=n(n−1)(n+2). Are there only finitely many integer triples n_(1),n_(2),n_(3)≥2 satisfying [F(n_(1))+F(n_(2))−F(n_(3))]^(2)=4F(n_(1))F(n_(2))?

auxiliary_results.statement: For sorted resonances, b<4F(a)/9 and c<a+b. In the box 2<=a<=b<c<=1000000 exactly (5,5,8),(10,10,16) occur.
changed_assumptions: All indices bounded by 1000000 for the finite classification.

targets.exact_retained_statement: What is the reverse-mathematical strength over RCA₀ of the assertion: for every commutative ring R, finite m×n matrix A over R and nonzero b∈R^m, if Ax=b has no constant solution, some finite coloring of R has no monochromatic solution?

auxiliary_results.statement: Over RCA0, WKL0 implies the ring-coloring assertion, with q(n)=[3(n-1)]^(n-1) colors for n>=2. The finite feasibility lemma is proved by explicit integer-matrix diagonalization.
changed_assumptions: Only the upper logical bound is proved.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Do absolute C,K>0 satisfy ω(G_p)≤C(log p)^K for every prime p≡1 mod 4?

auxiliary_results.statement: For every prime p congruent to 1 mod 4, global clique theta, global Schrijver clique theta, and degree-2 SOS all equal sqrt(p).

targets.exact_retained_statement: Does some ε>0 satisfy SOS₄(G_p)=O(p^{1/2−ε}) as p→∞ through primes p≡1 mod 4?

auxiliary_results.statement: For every finite vertex-transitive graph G, SOS4(G)<=1+theta(complement of its neighborhood graph). In particular this holds for every Paley G_p.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Do absolute C,α>0 and 0<δ<√2−1 exist such that (1−δ)||x||₂²≤||Φ_px||₂²≤(1+δ)||x||₂² for every x supported on at most Cp/(log p)^α coordinates and all sufficiently large such p?

auxiliary_results.statement: For every eligible p and integer 1<=k<=p+1, delta_k=(k-1)/sqrt(p) iff k<=omega(G_p)+1. If k>=omega+2 then delta_k<=min(1,(k-4+sqrt(k^2+4k-12))/(2sqrt(p))).

targets.exact_retained_statement: Do absolute C,K>0 satisfy ω(G_p)≤C(log p)^K for every prime p≡1 mod 4?
Does some ε>0 satisfy SOS₄(G_p)=O(p^{1/2−ε}) as p→∞ through primes p≡1 mod 4?
Are there infinitely many such p with 1+τ₊(H_p)<⌊(1+√(2p−1))/2⌋?
Does there exist ε>0 such that θ(H_p)≤(1/√2−ε)√p for all sufficiently large primes p≡1 mod 4?

auxiliary_results.statement: Exact finite results for all 29 primes p<=300, p congruent to 1 mod4, as enumerated in verification.json.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Do absolute C,α>0 and 0<δ<√2−1 exist such that (1−δ)||x||₂²≤||Φ_px||₂²≤(1+δ)||x||₂² for every x supported on at most Cp/(log p)^α coordinates and all sufficiently large such p?

auxiliary_results.statement: Theorem 18 and the quantitative Conjecture29 in Satake2405.08608v2 have stronger RIP-constant hypotheses than retained Q2191 and cannot be imported merely by citation substitution.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every separable f∈Z[x] of degree≥4 with no fixed prime-square divisor, is #{1≤n≤X:f(n) squarefree}∼X∏_{p prime}(1−ρ_f(p²)/p²)?

auxiliary_results.statement: Correct squarefree Euler-product asymptotics for pairwise coprime separable factors imply the correct asymptotic for their finite product.
changed_assumptions: Constituent asymptotics are hypotheses; the transfer implication is unconditional.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every separable f∈Z[x] of degree≥4 with c_f>0, is N_f(X)∼c_f X/log X?

auxiliary_results.statement: The analogous transfer holds at prime arguments using constituent prime asymptotics; f=x(x+1)(x^2+1) has no fixed square divisor but only prime argument2 gives a squarefree value.
changed_assumptions: Prime constituent asymptotics are required. The example has zero prime local constant and is not a Q1510 counterexample.

targets.exact_retained_statement: If R⊆N satisfies |(R△Q)∩[1,X]|=o(√X) as X→∞, is it impossible to have R=A+B with A,B⊆N and |A|,|B|≥2?

auxiliary_results.statement: Any retained near-square decomposition has E(X)>>_eta X^(1/3-eta) for every eta>0; hence perturbations O(X^(1/3-delta)) with delta>0 cannot decompose.
changed_assumptions: Stronger error restriction for the irreducibility corollary.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every n,m>1, is the non-cyclotomic part of Φ_n(x)+Φ_m(x) either 2 or irreducible?

auxiliary_results.statement: The retained noncyclotomic-sum conclusion holds whenever n and m are powers of two.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every n,m>1, is the non-cyclotomic part of Φ_n(x)Φ_m(x)+1 irreducible?

auxiliary_results.statement: Phi_n(x)^2+1 is irreducible when n is a power of two.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every finite nonempty L⊆{2,3,…}, does some A∈P satisfy L(A)=L?

auxiliary_results.statement: Every singleton length set {k}, k>=2, is realized; all65536 finite subsets of [0,16] containing0 were exhausted and seven displayed length-set witnesses independently checked.
changed_assumptions: Finite search bound max(A)<=16; general theorem treats singleton length sets.

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every prime p, does a constant c(p) bound the number of nonzero base-p digits of deg(f)+1 whenever f∈ℤ[x] splits over ℚ and no coefficient is divisible by p? Can c(p)=p−1 always be used?

auxiliary_results.statement: Exact reduction to split finite-field polynomials with every coefficient nonzero; if all roots have one nonzero residue class, degree+1 has exactly one nonzero base-p digit. This includes all of p=2.
changed_assumptions: One root residue class, or p=2.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Are there only finitely many Q-isomorphism classes of fields K with [K:Q]∈{6,7} and M(K)>7?

auxiliary_results.statement: M(K)<=#(O_K/p) for every prime ideal; resulting residue-degree restrictions above2,3,5,7 are necessary for M(K)>7, including unramified2 in degree7.
changed_assumptions: Necessary conditions, not field finiteness.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Is E(G)=d(G)+|G| for every finite nonabelian group G?

auxiliary_results.statement: E(G)>=d(G)+|G| for every finite group.
changed_assumptions: Only one inequality.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Does a cancellative torsion-free commutative monoid M with rank-one Grothendieck group exist such that M is almost atomic but P_fin(M) is not?

auxiliary_results.statement: Groups and nonnegative rank-one monoids with a positive lower gap have atomic finite power monoids. A counterexample must be a proper Puiseux monoid accumulating at0.
changed_assumptions: Excludes only the specified cases.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Does x⁴+x³y−y⁴+y³z+z⁴=0 have a solution (x,y,z)≠(0,0,0)?

auxiliary_results.statement: The quartic has a primitive Z_p point for every prime and a real point. Thus no modulus obstructs primitive solvability.
changed_assumptions: Local and real solvability; global rational/integer existence not established.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Does x³+x+y³+y+z³+z=xyz+1 have an integer solution?

auxiliary_results.statement: (-13/20,-79/20,21/5) is a rational point; integral local points exist for every prime; any integer point has every coordinate odd and none 0,+1,-1.
changed_assumptions: Rational and local solvability; no integer point supplied.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Is {(x,y,z,t):xyz+t²+1=0} a finite union of polynomial families?

auxiliary_results.statement: The displayed three-parameter polynomial family is Zariski dense but misses (-13,13,29,70), as do all of its sign/permutation copies.
changed_assumptions: One specified family, not arbitrary finite unions.

targets.exact_retained_statement: Are the only solutions of (a³+1)(b³+1)=x² the triples (1,23,156), (6,26, 1953), and (20,362,616077)?
Are the only solutions of (a³−1)(b³−1)=x² the triples (2,4,21), (2,22,273), (3,313,28236), and (4,22,819)?

auxiliary_results.statement: For b<=10000000 the retained lists are complete under 1<=a<b (plus) and 1<a<b (minus).

targets.exact_retained_statement: For every integer k>1, is (x,y,z)=(k−1,1,2) the only positive-integer solution of x²+(2k−1)^y=k^z?

auxiliary_results.statement: No positive solution exists for y in {3,5} and either even z or square k; the source gap-polynomial threshold is repaired and fully checked.

experiments.purpose: Find an explicit high-density coloring; no upper-bound or optimality claim.
experiments.domain: Piecewise constant colorings with interval and residue classes; exact final family has nine intervals.
experiments.generator: Seeded local improvement in rainbow_search.py and rainbow_grid_search.cpp; rational stationary calculation in rainbow_exact.py.
experiments.permitted_observations: Color assignments and exact or numerical counts of rainbow triples.
experiments.resource_budget: Initial parity grid240 with30 restarts and100 sweeps; saved C++ grid runs use120 or500 restarts,180 sweeps, and25-second per-run cap.
experiments.controls: Exact Fraction integration; symbolic integer all-t coefficients; independent integer rectangle enumeration and2548 brute-force cases.
experiments.uncertainty: Heuristic search is incomplete; the displayed coloring is rigorously certified without assuming the search was optimal.

primary_sources.finding: Retains polylogarithmic clique target and polynomial degree-four SOS improvement; proves relaxation lower bound c*p^(1/3). Proof not independently audited.
One-local circulant Fourier LP; source table already includes strict numerical improvements at p=61 and 281.
Two-local theta constant target remains conjectural in this source.
Dated 2026 restatement of main Paley targets, not a current-resolution certificate.
Original Conjecture 25 is fixed-delta near-linear sparsity, as retained in Q2191. Initial coherence-saturation identity is Theorem 20.

Theorem 18 assumes polynomial decay of the RIP constant. Conjecture 29 gives a stronger quantitative delta_K profile than the fixed-delta statement in the original cited Conjecture 25. Those profiles cannot be silently substituted for Q2191.
